drills.label: Cold open
drills.question_line: SAM: Before anything else, an item. A team runs a customer-support agent that can read tickets, draft replies
drills.answer_line: SAM: Model size has nothing to do with authorization scope.
drills.stem: A customer-support agent can read tickets, draft replies, issue refunds and delete user accounts. Support staff only ever read tickets and draft replies. Applying least privilege, which change best reduces risk?

options.A: Add logging to the refund and delete tools so misuse can be audited later
options.B: Remove the refund and delete tools from the agent's configuration
options.C: Keep all the tools but add a confirmation prompt before refunds and deletions
options.D: Replace the agent with a larger model that follows instructions more reliably

drills.why: Least privilege means the capability is gone, so the attack surface is gone. Logging is detective, confirmation is a speed bump, and model size is not authorization scope.

drills.label: Sample item
drills.question_line: SAM: An application sends the same eight-thousand-token system prompt and policy document on every request
drills.answer_line: ALEX: Constraint words: "same on every request", "both latency and cost"
drills.stem: An application sends the same 8,000-token system prompt and policy document on every request, followed by a short user message that changes each time. Latency and cost are both concerns. Which optimization most directly addresses both?

options.A: Truncate the policy document to the first 1,000 tokens
options.B: Switch to the smallest available model regardless of task fit
options.C: Put the static system prompt and policy before the dynamic content and enable prompt caching
options.D: Move the policy document into a few-shot example block

drills.why: Caching keys off a stable prefix: fixed content first, varying content after. A cache hit cuts input cost on the reused part and reduces time to first token.

drills.label: Sample item
drills.question_line: SAM: A rag system suddenly returns confident but incorrect answers after a document refresh. Latency and model
drills.answer_line: ALEX: Trigger: document refresh. Component it touched: the index. B.
drills.stem: A RAG system suddenly returns confident but incorrect answers after a document refresh. Latency and model version are unchanged. What is the most likely first place to investigate?

options.A: The model weights have silently changed
options.B: The retrieval or indexing step is returning irrelevant or stale chunks
options.C: The temperature setting is too low

drills.why: The refresh touched the index. Unchanged model version kills A; nothing about a refresh changes temperature or the context window.
